claims.summary: For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2, with probability tending to one, for every j with 1 <= j <= l_1 (the Leighton-Shor scale) and every bounded G Lipschitz on each open cell of mesh 2^(-j): |sum_i G(X_i) - N int G| <= L sqrt N (j^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) V_j(E_j G) + L sqrt(N log N) Lambda_j(G), E_j G the cell averages, V_j their cell variation, Lambda_j(G) the sum over cells Q of Lip(G on Q) times area(Q); for Lipschitz G, V_j(E_j G) <= 8 int(|d_1 G| + |d_2 G|). Corollary at (4,4), against Lebesgue measure: if int sum psi*_4(|d_i G|) <= 2 and each |d_i G| is 0 or in [y, 2y] with e^16 <= y <= 2^(l_1), then for every j <= j* = min(l_1, floor((log N)^(2/3)(log y)^(1/3))) the discrepancy is at most L sqrt(N log N)(1 + y area(U_j)), U_j the cells on which G is not constant; so L(1+K) sqrt(N log N) when area(U_j) <= K area(supp grad G).
claims.assessment: Working proof: split into cell averages, bounded by lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (b), (c) and its corollary, and a remainder bounded cell by cell by Theorem 4.5.3 of Talagrand's monograph rescaled to the cell, bounded differences and Chernoff, with a union bound over at most 2N cells; the corollary from psi*_4(x) >= x (log x)^(1/4)/2 for x >= e^16.
claims.rationale: Bounds, against Lebesgue measure and at order sqrt(N log N), the discrepancy of single-gradient-level class functions at (4,4) whose support is thick at the mesh 2^(-j*); isolates thin supports, level mixing and the conversion to the cell-smeared measures as the open cases.
claims.next_action: A version of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy for cell functions on a quadtree partition, to adapt the mesh to the gradient level.

relationships: Its parts (b), (c) and corollary bound the cell-averaged part.
Bounds at the conjectured order, against Lebesgue measure, single-level class functions at (4,4) with supports thick at the mesh 2^(-j*); the conversion to the class's smeared measures is not done.
